# Electronics — category guidance (auto-generated from live market data, 2026-08-26)

## Price sanity (NPR, live market data)
- Other Electronics: typically around 3,800, most listings 900–30,000 (180 listings)
- Cameras, Camcorders & Accessories: typically around 6,500, most listings 2,800–52,000 (79 listings)
- Audio & Sound Systems: typically around 1,200, most listings 500–11,500 (63 listings)
- Laptop & Computer Accessories: typically around 4,500, most listings 1,200–32,000 (53 listings)
- Desktop Computers: typically around 8,000, most listings 450–34,000 (25 listings)
- Home Appliances: typically around 3,500, most listings 1,000–40,000 (24 listings)
- ACs & Home Electronics: typically around 1,150, most listings 500–5,000 (20 listings)
- Laptops: typically around 25,000, most listings 12,000–180,000 (18 listings)
- Tablets & Accessories: typically around 5,500, most listings 750–30,000 (14 listings)
- Video Game Consoles & Accessories: typically around 10,000, most listings 1,500–86,000 (6 listings — thin)
- Photocopiers: typically around 15,000, most listings 9,000–30,000 (5 listings — thin)
- TV & Video Accessories: typically around 18,000, most listings 17,000–52,000 (3 listings — thin)

For high-value gear here (laptops, cameras/lenses, drones, consoles), a price far below the
low end — e.g. a "brand new" flagship laptop at NPR 5,000 — is a scam signal: hold. Where marked
thin (n < 10) the data is weak; lean on general market judgment. Several subcategories mix
accessories with full devices (a NPR 500 "Desktop Computers" listing is likely a part, not a PC),
so judge the price against what is actually being sold, not the subcategory name alone.

## What good listings look like
- "Tamron 70-180mm F2.8 G2 Sony E-Mount Telephoto Lens" — NPR 137,000
- "Dahua Hero A1 Wireless Surveillance Camera" — NPR 6,500
- "DJI MINI 2 PRO KO BATTERY" — NPR 5,000
- "JBL go 3 speaker" — NPR 600
- "Nintendo gamecube" — NPR 10,000

A good listing names brand + model plus one key spec (lens mount, MP, capacity, condition).
Mixed English/romanized-Nepali wording ("ko", "on sale") is normal here, not a quality problem.

## Category-specific hold signals
- Product details that contradict the named item (wrong model's specs, outdated or copied
  product info) — the one recorded editor rejection in this category was exactly this.
- Sealed/"brand new" premium gear (AirPods, DJI drones, flagship cameras, consoles) priced far
  below its range above — the classic bait / advance-payment scam pattern in Nepal.
